1.1: Dhritarashtra's opening question — a blind king asking what his sons did, betraying that he already fears the answer.
1.2: Sanjaya begins: Duryodhana, seeing the Pandava army arrayed, goes to his teacher — anxiety dressed as protocol.
1.3: Duryodhana points out the enemy formation to Drona, needling him about the disciple who built it.
1.4: Duryodhana names the great archers on the other side — the list itself shows how rattled he is.
1.5: More Pandava heroes named; the recitation is a man reassuring himself by counting the threat.
1.6: Still naming warriors — Abhimanyu and the sons of Draupadi, all mighty chariot-fighters.
1.7: Now he turns to his own side, asking Drona to note the distinguished leaders of his army.
1.8: Duryodhana lists his own champions: Bhishma, Karna, Kripa, Ashwatthama and others.
1.9: Many more are ready to lay down their lives for him, armed and skilled in war.
1.10: Duryodhana weighs the two armies and admits his own, though led by Bhishma, feels insufficient.
1.11: Duryodhana orders his troops to guard Bhishma at every point of the formation.
1.12: Bhishma roars and blows his conch to lift Duryodhana's spirits — the elder steadying the anxious.
1.13: Conches, drums and horns erupt together; the sound of the Kaurava side is tumultuous.
1.14: Krishna and Arjuna, in a chariot drawn by white horses, blow their divine conches in reply.
1.15: The names of the conches are given — Panchajanya, Devadatta, Paundra — each blown by its warrior.
1.16: Yudhishthira, Nakula and Sahadeva sound theirs; the roll call continues.
1.17: Other great bowmen — Kashiraja, Shikhandi, Dhrishtadyumna, Satyaki — join the sound.
1.18: Drupada, Draupadi's sons and Abhimanyu blow their conches; the whole army answers.
1.19: The uproar shakes earth and sky and tears the hearts of Dhritarashtra's sons.
1.20: With the battle about to begin, Arjuna lifts his bow and prepares to shoot.
1.21: Arjuna asks Krishna to place the chariot between the two armies — the request that changes everything.
1.22: Arjuna wants to see who has come to fight, and with whom he must contend.
1.23: Arjuna wishes to look at those assembled to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra.
1.24: Sanjaya reports that Krishna does exactly as asked, drawing up the chariot between the armies.
1.25: Krishna places him before Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, and says: behold these Kurus.
1.26: Arjuna looks and sees fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons and friends — not enemies.
1.27: Seeing all his kinsmen arrayed, he is overcome with deep compassion and speaks in sorrow.
1.28: The collapse begins: seeing his own people ready to fight, his limbs give way and his mouth dries.
1.29: Arjuna's body trembles, his hair stands on end, the bow slips from his hand and his skin burns.
1.30: Arjuna cannot stand; his mind reels; he sees only ill omens — a clinical picture of panic.
1.31: Arjuna sees no good in killing his own people, and wants neither victory nor kingdom nor pleasure.
1.32: What use is a kingdom, or enjoyment, or life itself, to those for whom he wanted them?
1.33: The very people for whose sake wealth is desired are standing here, staking their lives.
1.34: Teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers, uncles, in-laws and kinsmen — all of them.
1.35: Arjuna will not kill them even to gain the three worlds, let alone this earth.
1.36: What joy could come from killing Dhritarashtra's sons? Only sin would fall upon him.
1.37: Killing one's own kin cannot bring happiness; they are family, however wrong they are.
1.38: Though the others, blinded by greed, see no fault in destroying family and betraying friends —
1.39: — why should we, who do see the evil in it, not turn away from this crime?
1.40: When a family is destroyed its immemorial dharma perishes, and lawlessness overtakes the rest.
1.41: With lawlessness the women are corrupted, and from that corruption comes confusion of lineage.
1.42: That confusion drags the family and its destroyers to hell, and the ancestral rites fail.
1.43: By these crimes the enduring practices of family and caste are wiped out.
1.44: Those whose family dharma is destroyed dwell in hell — this is what he has heard.
1.45: Arjuna recoils: we are prepared to commit a great sin out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom.
1.46: Better that the armed Kauravas kill him unresisting and unarmed than that he fight.
1.47: Arjuna casts away his bow and arrows and sinks down in the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
